issue: fs.readFile on every GET /api/feature-flags request — disk I/O on hot path
estimated_impact: +2-5ms p50 latency per request; under concurrent load, filesystem contention adds +10-50ms p95
recommendation: Cache features.json in memory with TTL (e.g. 5s), invalidate on write. Or load once at startup and refresh on POST.

issue: Second fs.readFile for GET /api/feature-flags/:name — same file read again for single feature lookup
evidence: const raw = await fs.readFile(FEATURES_PATH, 'utf8') — called on every single-feature request
estimated_impact: Same as above. Doubled I/O if client fetches list then individual features.
recommendation: Share cached data between routes. Single in-memory cache for features.json.

issue: Read-modify-write cycle on features.json for every state change — no caching
evidence: fs.readFile + JSON.parse + modify + JSON.stringify + fs.writeFile on every POST /state
estimated_impact: +5-15ms per write operation; under concurrent writes, file corruption risk
recommendation: Use in-memory state with periodic flush, or migrate to database storage.

issue: GET /api/orders returns ALL orders without pagination
evidence: const orders = await Order.find({}).populate('user', 'id name') — no .limit() or .skip()
estimated_impact: With 10K orders: +500ms-2s response time, +5-20MB memory per request, MongoDB cursor overhead
recommendation: Add pagination like productController: pageSize + skip + countDocuments.

issue: GET /api/orders/myorders returns ALL user orders without pagination
evidence: const orders = await Order.find({ user: req.user._id }) — no limit
estimated_impact: Heavy user with 500+ orders: +100-300ms, growing memory usage

issue: GET /api/users returns ALL users without pagination
evidence: const users = await User.find({}) — no limit or skip
estimated_impact: With 100K users: +2-5s response, +50MB+ memory. Admin-only endpoint but still problematic.
recommendation: Add pagination. Even admin endpoints need bounded responses.

issue: Product review duplicate check loads entire product with all reviews
evidence: const product = await Product.findById(req.params.id) — loads all reviews into memory to check if user already reviewed
estimated_impact: Product with 1000 reviews: ~200KB loaded into memory. O(N) scan for duplicate check.
recommendation: Use MongoDB query: Product.findOne({ _id: req.params.id, 'reviews.user': req.user._id }) to check without loading all reviews.

issue: GET /api/products/top queries and sorts DB on every request
estimated_impact: Full collection scan + sort on every request. With 10K products: +50-200ms p95
recommendation: Cache top products with TTL (e.g. 5 min). Data changes infrequently.

issue: Entire Qdrant corpus loaded into memory and cached globally forever
evidence: _CORPUS global variable — _load_corpus() scrolls ALL documents and keeps them in memory permanently
estimated_impact: With 10K chunks × 1KB avg: ~10MB base + tokenized copies. Grows with corpus size, never freed.
recommendation: Add TTL or LRU eviction. Or reconsider BM25 approach to use Qdrant's built-in full-text search.

issue: Order.find({ user: req.user._id }) likely missing compound index
evidence: Filtering orders by user — if no index on { user: 1 }, full collection scan

issue: Synchronous file read in MCP server on every tool call
evidence: with FEATURES_PATH.open('r', encoding='utf-8') as fh: return json.load(fh)
estimated_impact: +1-3ms per MCP call. Low traffic so minimal real impact.
recommendation: Cache with TTL for read-heavy patterns.

issue: BM25 search recomputes IDF and term frequencies on every query
evidence: _bm25_search recalculates term_doc_freq from entire corpus for every search call
estimated_impact: With 5K documents: +20-50ms per search. Proportional to corpus size.
recommendation: Pre-compute IDF values when corpus is loaded. Cache term_doc_freq.
